result.summary: Splits block index synchronization into parallel block digestion and sequential post-processing phases, and introduces a general-purpose ThreadPool utility. Indexes that implement concurrent digestion (currently blockfilterindex and txindex) can process batches of blocks across multiple worker threads during initial sync when enabled via the new `-indexworkers=<n>` startup option.
result.problem: Constructing block filter and transaction indexes during initial sync is slow because blocks, undo data, and headers are read from disk and processed sequentially one block at a time on a single thread.
evidence: Author benchmark from the PR description: 'with the node in debug mode and on IBD, with -indexworkers=4, the block filter index generation took less than an hour. While, in master, the sync took more than 7 hours.'
result.scope_notes: The PR introduces a new general-purpose `ThreadPool` class in `src/util/threadpool.h` with dedicated unit and fuzz tests, in addition to the indexing changes. Part of the `BaseIndex` sync loop refactor in `src/index/base.cpp` was truncated from the patch snippet.
result.card: Parallelizes initial block indexing across multiple worker threads for the compact block filter and transaction indexes, configured by a new `-indexworkers=<n>` flag. Today, initial index builds are strictly single-threaded and read blocks and undo data sequentially from disk, causing initial sync to take many hours. The author reports that building the block filter index took under 1 hour with 4 workers compared to over 7 hours on master. Work is related to and proceeding alongside PR #34489.
